 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. On Wednesday afternoon, a free agent deal between Dustin May and the Chicago White Sox became official for three years and $52.5 million .
 Because of May's addition, the White Sox were forced to make a corresponding move with their 40-man roster, which was completely full. Chicago decided to designate right-handed pitcher Jordan Leasure for assignment.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It's a decision that shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone. Leasure seriously regressed in the early stages of 2026, struggling to a 6.27 ERA over 18 appearances out of the White Sox bullpen.
 He's now 28 years old and suffered a season-ending injury in May that will also force him to miss the entire 2027 season.
 On May 29, the White Sox placed Leasure on the 15-day injured list with a right flexor strain before promptly transferring him to the 60-day IL. In August, it became evident that Leasure needed surgery. He underwent Tommy John surgery to repair his torn UCL and will now miss all of 2027 while hoping to be healthy again for spring training in 2028.
 Leasure has a big fastball, which has always been a productive pitch for him. He gets good extension, uses his 6-foot-3 frame well, and induces plenty of chases out of the zone and whiffs. Control has always been an issue, though, as has the home run ball.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement During his 18.2 big league innings in 2026, Leasure allowed six home runs and issued eight walks. Not exactly a successful recipe for a relief pitcher. It was an overall discouraging regression for a guy who ranked in the 96th percentile among pitchers in expected batting average against (.190 xBA) and posted a 3.19 xERA in 2025.
 There was a time when Leasure looked like a legitimate closer option for the Sox , especially given the swing-and-miss potential of his fastball, but the inconsistency of his command and his inability to limit hard contact have prevented him from establishing himself as a reliable late-inning option.
 Now, with a lengthy injury recovery ahead of him, his future in the organization is more uncertain than ever.
 At this stage, I'm not sure the White Sox are losing much in the bullpen based on what we saw from Leasure in 2026. For a team with aspirations of contending in 2027, they need more reliable arms, especially in high-leverage situations.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It's highly unlikely that anybody will claim Leasure and add him to their 40-man roster at this stage of the offseason. That likely means the White Sox will have the opportunity to keep him in the organization as he recovers.
 For the time being, though, it was a relatively easy DFA decision for the Sox.
